prompt: Line $\ell$ has equation $5x - 2y = 8$. Line $m$ is perpendicular to $\ell$ and passes through the point $(5, 1)$. What is the $y$-intercept of line $m$?
hint: Find the slope of $\ell$ first, then take the negative reciprocal.

hints.text: Find the slope of $\ell$ first, then take the negative reciprocal.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easier line: $\ell$ is $y = 2x$, so $m$ has slope $-\tfrac{1}{2}$. Through $(2, 3)$: $3 = -1 + b$, so $b = 4$. Same three moves — convert, flip-and-negate, substitute.

learningObjective: Chain the perpendicular condition with point substitution.
explanation: Rewrite $\ell$: $-2y = -5x + 8$, so $y = \tfrac{5}{2}x - 4$ and its slope is $\tfrac{5}{2}$.
Perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal: $-\tfrac{2}{5}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Three separate places to lose this question
steps: First, dividing by $-2$ and forgetting to flip both signs — the slope of $\ell$ is $+\tfrac{5}{2}$, not $-\tfrac{5}{2}$.
Second, flipping without negating for the perpendicular slope.
Third, stopping at the equation instead of reading off the intercept. Naming the three checkpoints as you go is how you keep a multi-step question clean.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Flipping without negating gives slope +2/5 and b = −1; negating without flipping gives −5/2 and a different wrong b.
Run the two-part rule out loud — flip it, negate it — then confirm the product of the slopes is −1 before substituting the point.
